title: Seminar invitation with President Stone and BS Sweden
content:
Blue Shield Sweden is inviting you to a seminar on Protection of Cultural Heritage in Crisis with Peter Stone, President of Blue Shield

Date: September 9th, 2025
Time: 3.00 pm to 6.00 pm. CEST
Place: Hybrid – Online/Medelhavsmuseet, Stockholm, Sweden
Language: English

How do we protect our common Cultural Heritage? What concrete experiences and good examples are there internationally – and what can Sweden learn from these?

Blue Shield Sweden invites you to a seminar on this urgent matter with Professor Peter Stone, President of Blue Shield.

Together with decision-makers, experts, individuals and organisations from the cultural and defence sectors, we intend to discuss what better protection could be like in a Swedish context and how increased coordination, both nationally and internationally, is crucial.

  • Welcome and introduction
  • Presentation by Peter Stone
  • Remarks by Ukrainian colleagues
  • Panel discussion with representatives from Swedish authorities involved in efforts to strengthen protection of cultural heritage
  • Social gathering

    • The number of in person seats is limited – registration will be required for in person attendance and to receive the online link.

    Kind regards

    The board of

title: “Strengthen Appreciation”: Malians celebrate at Tomb of Askia
content:
Restoration work has been ongoing at the Tomb of Askia. They were honored by a visit from the Mayor, who received a celebratory plaque on the restoration work.

On 5th May, the Mali Committee of the Blue Shield celebrated African World Heritage Day in Gao with celebrations at  the site of the 15th Century Tomb of Askia.  Mamadou Samaké, President of Blue Shield Mali, is the Site Manager , and the visit was carried out in partnership with the National Committee.

It was a wonderful way to raise awareness about the importance of the site.

title: Happy Anniversary to our National Committees
content:
This year we are celebrating the 25th anniversary of the founding of our first national committees!

In 2000, the first national committees were founded, and Blue Shield became a truly worldwide organisation, protecting heritage in crisis.

The Blue Shield was founded in 1996 by the Executive Boards of the International Council on Archives (ICA); International Council of Museums (ICOM); International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA); and International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS). with the goal of protecting heritage in conflict, disaster, and complex emergencies. Marie-Therese Varlamoff, the then Director of IFLA Preservation and Conservation Core Activity, campaigned worldwide for national committees, recognising the need to parallel the Red Cross.  Her efforts quickly paid off, and Blue Shield soon saw the foundation of national committees in The Netherlands, Great Britain & Ireland (joint committee), France, Belgium and Norway. Poland and Czechia quickly followed.

Today we have 34 National Committees around the world, and more in development, all working for the vital protection of cultural property in support of affected communities!

title: BS Ireland works with Irish Red Cross
content:
Blue Shield Ireland was honoured to have two representatives serving as judges for the Corn Adomnáin International Humanitarian Law Competition organised by the Irish Red Cross and hosted by Queens University, Belfast. Blue Shield partnered with the National Advisory Committee on Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict to judge the Cultural Property scenario of the competition and to award the prize for best performance in the category. The Irish National Committee of the Blue Shield would like to congratulate the winning team from the Law Society of Ireland.

title: BS Poland supports Safe cultural heritage — European challenges in times of war and crisis
content:
On 3 and 4 April 2025, the International Forum “Safe cultural heritage — European challenges in times of war and crisis” was held in Kraków, Poland. The event, organised by the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage and the Ministry of the Interior and Administration, was a meeting of experts from across Europe who discussed the key challenges of protecting cultural heritage in crises.

Blue Shield Poland was proud to support this excellent event. Krzysztof Sałaciński, President of the Polish Blue Shield Committee, moderated the panel: Heritage in the Face of Information Warfare and Armed Conflict.

This prestigious event is part of the activities undertaken under the Polish presidency of the Council of the European Union, and it aims to exchange experience, present good practices and develop common solutions for the protection of cultural heritage in situations of threat, both of war and crisis.

title: BS Belgium joins LUX response network
content:
Blue Shield Belgium is excited to announce that it has joined the LUX response programme. LUX response is an initiative that pools knowledge and actions, and brings together key players to better prevent and manage crises. This network – in which Blue Shield Belgium represents the heritage sector – is made up of experts from a variety of sectors who can be mobilised to respond to a crisis. The working methodology of LUX response is based on the recommendations of the founding texts (UN Sendai Framework, NATO Baselines, the White Book: Recommendations for improving crisis management in Belgium, and the Report of the Walloon Parliamentary Commission following the floods of 2021).

Blue Shield Belgium President, Gustaaf Janssens, and the Governor of the Province of Luxembourg, Olivier Schmitz, signed an initial agreement on 4 June 2024; a second agreement followed as part of the integration of Blue Shield Belgium into the LUX response programme.

The first meeting of the LUX response steering committee took place in February 2025.

title: BS UK Webinar series on conflict and the 1954 Hague Convention
content:
The Blue Shield UK Conflict & Military Activity Working Group is hosting a free series of webinars about conflict and the risks to UK heritage, your obligations under the 1954 Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict – and how you can prepare your institutions for these risks.

It will be hosted on

  • the third Friday of every month from March to December 2025 (excepting August)
  • 12.30-13.00 (Individual seminar times may change.)
  • on Zoom.

    • All are welcome to attend, but especially heritage professionals, students, and members of the armed services.

    The link to register can be found here:
    ​https://forms.office.com/e/whZtmimcXn

title: Saving heritage in Mayotte
content:
Tropical Cyclone Chido was a compact but very powerful, destructive, and deadly tropical cyclone which impacted Southeast Africa in December 2024, hitting the islands of Mayotte on 14 December. 

Heritage agencies began sharing reports of the damage (shared via Blue Shield France) on 1 January, reporting damage to archives and museums, and calling for aid. Blue Shield France quickly launched an Appeal for aid. 

Two volunteers  – Charlotte and Emmanuel – went to help the Museum of Mayotte. Blue Shield France is an accredited disaster response agency with the French government: their volunteers are rigorously trained. The deployed volunteers stayed in a base camp with other emergency responders.

title: Seven Recommendations for implementing the 1954 Hague Convention
content:
On 2 July 2024, Blue Shield Austria, Blue Shield Germany, and partners had the privilege of hosting the 70th Anniversary Event of the 1954 Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict at the Permanent Representation of Austria to the EU in Brussels.

The event titled “Milestones & Way to Go” brought together experts from the European Union, the Defense Sector, and Non-Governmental Organisations, including Blue Shield International, to discuss how we can collectively strengthen the protection of cultural property during armed conflicts and disasters.

Through interdisciplinary dialogue, they have developed Seven Recommendations focused on integrating the 1954 Hague Convention and its Protocols into EU policies to:

  • Strengthen the EU’s global commitment to safeguarding cultural heritage.
  • Align cultural property protection efforts with EU policies to promote resilience.
  • Protect critical infrastructure essential for preserving cultural heritage.

    • Explore these proposals: they welcome any opportunity to collaborate, discuss, or provide further input.
